title: Spiral reading order
prompt:
A display panel is drawn by a pen that starts at the top-left cell and moves clockwise around the edge, then spirals inward until every cell has been visited once. Given the panel as a grid of numbers, return the cell values in the order the pen visits them.

- grid has 1 to 100 rows and 1 to 100 columns, and every row has the same length.
- Values are integers between -100 and 100.
hints: Keep four bounds: top, bottom, left and right. Each lap walks the top row, right column, bottom row and left column.
After a lap, move every bound one step inward.
When only one row or one column is left, walking back along the bottom or up the left would read cells twice. Check top < bottom and left < right first.

solution.explanation: Four bounds mark the unread ring. Each lap reads the top row left to right, the right column downwards, then, only if the ring has more than one row and column, the bottom row right to left and the left column upwards. Shrinking all four bounds moves to the next ring. Every cell is read exactly once.

complexity.notes: Each cell is visited once. Apart from the output list, only four bounds are stored. A direction-vector walk that marks visited cells also works but needs O(m × n) extra space.

followUps: Read the grid anticlockwise, starting at the top-right corner.
Fill an n × n grid with 1 to n² in spiral order.
